newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MATCH ANALYSIS OF BRAZIL V ITALY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MATCH ANALYSIS OF BRAZIL V ITALY.

text.p: A look at the strengths and weaknesses of Brazil and Italy ahead of their Tournoi de France match at Lyon's Gerland stadium on Sunday (kickoff 1830 GMT):

Playing style: Brazil under the hugely experienced Mario Zagallo are looking to return to their roots and play in the best traditions of the "beautiful game", as Pele called it. Zagallo believes he has the players to do this after a 1994 World Cup victory in which Carlos Parreira allied skill to a certain amount of pragmatism. He has recalled 33-year-old Dunga for his experience and perhaps until he finds another similar though younger candidate for the job of holding the midfield as a launch pad for the skills of the attackers. The defence, in typical Brazilian style, are there to block the opposition and join the attack whenever they can.

Strengths: The immense gifts of their outfield players starting with right back Cafu, passing through the ball skills of their midfielders to the match-winning potential of Romario and Ronaldo up front. Add the spice of their free-kick expertise, most notably that of left back Roberto Carlos, who put such a bend on the ball that he completely surprised France and all onlookers in the 1-1 draw on Tuesday. Unwavering confidence in their game.

Weaknesses: Lack of time training together, Zagallo saying he scrapped other plans in order to play in this tournament. A little-tested central defence partnership easily turned by quick strikers. Full backs who are better going forward than in defence.

Motivation: Individually, a place in the 1998 World Cup squad looking for a fifth crown and a second in a row. As a team, to continue to show they are the world's best, can remain so playing all out attacking football and -- in this match against Italy -- that they would have won the 1994 final if there had been a replay.
Team: Taffarel; Cafu, Celio Silva, Aldair, Roberto Carlos; Giovanni, Mauro Silva, Dunga, Leonardo; Ronaldo, Romario.

Italy Playing style: Cesare Maldini has gone back to a traditional Italian playing style since taking over from Arrigo Sacchi in December. Since the 1960s the most successful Italian teams have been based on rock-solid defending and while that is still the case there is plenty of flair, movement and pace in all departments of the team. Maldini played in a negative style against England on Wednesday, keeping seven or eight men behind the ball at times but their usual tactical ability on the ball let them down and they conceded two goals.

Strengths: Traditional Italian strengths include great defensive awareness, superbly gifted midfielders and front-runners full of flair, strength and speed. This team possesses all those qualities but whether they will be displayed to the full against Brazil is open to doubt.

Weaknesses: Going into Sunday's match, Italy seem unfocused and unmotivated. They have been hit by injuries to players such as Fabrizio Ravanelli and Roberto Baggio who are not with the squad, and Albertino Demetrio and Ciro Ferrara who played against England. Roberto di Matteo who limped off injured against England is also doubtful.

Motivation: Italy showed little interest against England. It remains to be seen whether their first meeting with Brazil since the 1994 World Cup Final will inspire them or whether their collective end-of-season lethargy will cause them to play well below par again.
